clue.text: Bed lad made up in bag for pig

indicators.note: in tells us the rearranged letters go inside the word for bag

parts.note: a sack is a bag

indicators.note: made up means put together anew, so the letters of bed lad are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young lad's bed is made up inside a bag, perhaps destined for a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made up' looks like bed-making, but it shuffles the letters of 'Bed lad'; 'in' places them within the bag word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Saddleback is a British breed of pig, black with a white band over its shoulders.

clue.text: Sport needing money getting nothing

parts.note: a sum is an amount of money
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A sport that needs funding but receives none.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumo is the Japanese wrestling sport of heavyweights.

clue.text: Eloquent speaker turning red with malice

indicators.note: turning means the letters of red and malice are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: An orator going red in the face with spite.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who declaims delivers rhetorical speeches, an orator.

clue.text: Silent actor excited Dolly

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters of Dolly are rearranged

explanation.surface: A silent-film star gets an actress called Dolly worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dolly' suggests Dolly Parton, but it is just the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Lloyd was a star comedian of silent films, famous for hanging from a clock face.

clue.text: Throwing poor actor out of former county town

indicators.note: out of means the bad performer's word is taken away from the town's name

parts.note: Buckingham was formerly the county town of Buckinghamshire, England
a ham is an overacting, poor actor

explanation.surface: A bad actor is being thrown out of an old English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Buckingham lost its county-town role to Aylesbury; HAM taken from it leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse bucking is throwing its rider off with leaping kicks.

clue.text: Old police sergeant involved in church work — retired from here?

indicators.note: involved in means the old sergeant's letters are placed within the church abbreviation

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A former police sergeant now busy with church work after leaving the force.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the rest of the clue: a police sergeant retires from the police station.
explanation.definitionFit: A cop shop is slang for a police station, the workplace an officer leaves on retirement.

clue.text: It's quiet in typical museum

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the words typical museum

explanation.surface: A typical museum is a quiet place.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm and quiet are synonyms for a peaceful, still state.

clue.text: Female with spite putting male off

indicators.note: putting a thing off means removing it, so the male's letter is taken away

parts.note: malice is spite

explanation.surface: A spiteful woman putting a man off.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice is a girl's name, so it can stand for a female.

clue.text: Law officer right to be included among 'wise men', say

parts.note: the Magi were the three wise men of the Nativity

indicators.note: to be included among means the letter for right is placed within the other words

parts.note: to state is to say

explanation.surface: A law officer is right to be counted among the wise, it is claimed.
explanation.definitionFit: A magistrate is a judicial officer who administers the law in lower courts.

clue.text: What one likes, but another one would be very different!

definitions.text: What one likes, but another one would be very different!

parts.words: What one likes, but another one would be very different!
parts.note: something you like is said to be your favourite drink, and 'another' of that drink is an idiom for a different matter entirely

explanation.surface: Musing that one person's preference would be quite unlike another's.
explanation.walkthrough: Two idioms: 'just my cup of tea' is what one likes, and 'another cup of tea altogether' means something very different.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is British idiom for something one enjoys, and with 'another' it means a different matter.

clue.text: Bill embraced by leader of China in region of that country

indicators.note: embraced by means the bill's letters are held within the leader's name

parts.note: Mao Zedong led communist China
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A bill is welcomed by China's leader in one of its regions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader of China' looks like the letter C, but it is Chairman Mao; 'that country' points back to China.
explanation.definitionFit: Macao is a special administrative region of China, a former Portuguese colony.

clue.text: Getting hold of top mathematician

parts.note: a cap is a top, as on a bottle
Alan Turing was the British mathematician and codebreaker

explanation.surface: Getting hold of a leading mathematician.
explanation.definitionFit: To capture is to seize or take hold of something.

clue.text: Smooth sorceress with no time for quick snack?

parts.note: to sand is to smooth

indicators.note: with no means the time letter is removed from the sorceress

parts.note: a witch is a sorceress

explanation.surface: A slick sorceress too busy for anything but a quick bite.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandwich is the classic snack eaten in a hurry; the question mark admits it is an example.

clue.text: Map-makers engaging chaps producing signs

indicators.note: engaging means taking in, so the chaps go inside the map-makers

parts.note: OS is the Ordnance Survey, Britain's national mapping agency
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Cartographers hiring men to make road signs.
explanation.definitionFit: Omens are portents, signs of what is to come.

clue.text: Cutlery may be so negotiable

definitions.meaning: knives and forks are laid out on the dining surface
open for discussion, as an offer put forward in talks

explanation.surface: Cutlery's placement could be up for negotiation.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid on the dining surface literally, and figuratively an offer open to discussion.

clue.text: Fellow at the entrance about to provide label with ID

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the doorkeeper's word is read backwards

parts.note: a gateman is a man who keeps a gate

explanation.surface: A doorman provides each visitor with a label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow at the entrance' is one word, GATEMAN, which 'about' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A name tag is a badge bearing the wearer's name for identification.

clue.text: Big female bird with a head buried

indicators.note: buried means the letter a is placed deep within the other pieces

parts.note: a tit is a small bird
a ness is a headland, a head

explanation.surface: A large female bird has its head buried, ostrich-style.
explanation.definitionFit: A titaness is a female Titan, a giantess of Greek myth, hence a big female.

clue.text: Baseball player in jug

definitions.meaning: the player who throws the ball to the batter

explanation.surface: A baseball player in a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a baseball thrower and a pouring vessel share this word.

clue.text: House I head — I love upsetting common folk

parts.note: the poll is the head, as in poll tax

indicators.note: upsetting in a down clue means turning over, so these letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: Someone running a household upsets the masses.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoi polloi is Greek for 'the many', used for the common people.

clue.text: Nelson maybe making short speech after end of skirmish

indicators.note: after means the speech comes after that final letter
end of picks the final letter of skirmish
short means the speech word loses its last letter

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: Nelson gives a brief speech after a battle ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio was Admiral Nelson's first name, so Nelson is one example bearing it.

clue.text: Penny's face maybe when old boy introduces poetry

indicators.note: introduces means the old boy comes first, ahead of the poetry

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: A girl called Penny looks on as an old schoolboy reads poems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a woman's name; it is the coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The obverse is the side of a coin bearing the head, so a penny's face.

clue.text: One without false ideas about top people

parts.note: re means about, concerning
the A-list is the elite, top celebrities

explanation.surface: Someone clear-sighted about celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist sees things as they are, free of illusions.

clue.text: Most naughty one in run on street

indicators.note: in means the letter for one goes inside the word for run

parts.note: to race is to run
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The naughtiest child running in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Racy means risqué, so the raciest is the naughtiest.

clue.text: Travel wearing metal cross

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the metal wraps around the travel word

parts.note: tin is a metal
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: Someone travelling in armour bearing a cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like an adjective or a crucifix; it is a hybrid animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tigon is the hybrid offspring of a tiger and a lioness, a cross.

clue.text: Van may have this protection behind

definitions.text: Van may have this protection behind

parts.words: Van may have this protection behind
parts.note: on British trains the rear van carried the official who watched over the train, and a defensive force at the back of an army also protects from behind

explanation.surface: A van might carry protection at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: The van is the rear carriage of an old British train, named after the official riding in it; the rear of an army is also protected by such a force.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means protection, and the official on a British train rode in the van at its rear.

clue.text: Animal and I getting round in vehicle for holiday

indicators.note: in means the animal, I and round go inside the vehicle

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
a cat is an animal
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A pet and its owner travel around in a van on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacation is the American word for a holiday break.

clue.text: Pet avoiding river in Greek valley

indicators.note: avoiding means keeping clear of, so the river letter is left out

parts.note: a pet is a fit of temper, a sulk

explanation.surface: A pet keeps away from the river in a Greek valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like an animal; it is a fit of pique.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vale of Tempe is a celebrated gorge in Thessaly, Greece.

clue.text: Group's joke entertaining any number

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the number goes inside the joke

parts.note: a gag is a joke
N stands for any number in maths

explanation.surface: A troupe's comedy routine pleases any number of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A gang is a group of people acting together.

clue.text: Restaurant making money by lake

parts.note: brass is slang for money
Lake Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A lakeside eatery turning a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: A brasserie is an informal French-style restaurant.

clue.text: Competent maiden making comeback as songstress

indicators.note: making a comeback means returning, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: able means competent
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A capable young singer returning to the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Nellie Melba was a renowned Australian soprano.

clue.text: Aims to finish before start of supper

indicators.note: before means the finish word comes ahead of the supper letter

parts.note: to end is to finish

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of supper

explanation.surface: Someone aims to wrap things up before supper starts.
explanation.definitionFit: Ends in the sense of goals or purposes, as in 'means to an end'.

clue.text: Being afraid about the cover bird has been given

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the fear word goes round the other word

parts.note: fearing means being afraid

explanation.surface: A frightened bird, nervous about its covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumage covering a bird is its feathering.
